why: Speculative decoding's speed follows how predictable the text is, so it is measured on natural requests, not token ids. A repetitive synthetic prompt once ranked k=3 above k=2 on the 27B AWQ (95 against 87 tok/s) where natural prompts ranked it below (81.6 against 88.6), docs/recommended-setup.md. Each prompt is sent as one user turn through the model's own chat template. Change the set only with a new version: measurements name the version and the set's sha256. Version 1 (8 prompts, data/mtp_prompts_v1.json, sha256 aba4e514...) is kept unchanged so its records stay readable, and is said underpowered when read; version 2 is its 8 prompts and 7 more, its size derived (size). Every prompt must naturally run past the timed tokens: a reply that ends early is refused (collectors/mtp.guard).
source: Every prompt written for BoltBeam by its authors (version 1 on 2026-11-08, the 7 added on 2026-11-12); none copied from a dataset. Natural requests only, one user turn each.

kinds_why.technical explanation, summary, comparis: version 1's kinds: what one person asks a local assistant to explain, write or plan
kinds_why.chat: the most common local use: an open question about one's own life, answered at length
kinds_why.code: a second code prompt (SQL with its example output): code is the other main local workload, and drafts differently from prose
kinds_why.multilingual (Spanish, Chinese): one Latin-script and one non-Latin-script language: a local user who writes in their own language; tokenizers split them differently, which moves acceptance
kinds_why.tool-style JSON: agent use: tool calls and structured output, each written as a task whose natural answer is long (a planned sequence of calls with reasons; a schema with examples), so the timed tokens are answer, not text after the end

size.effect_why: the step between adjacent draft counts the rule must tell apart: from k=3 up the measured steps ran -9.4% to +14.6%, median size 3.9% (29 steps, 2026-11-12, the 27B AWQ); 5% is the margin formula figures already carry (core/draft_count.FORMULA_TIE)
size.power_why: the share of real 5% steps the paired rule must call: 4 in 5, the usual choice. A missed step is not free: in the sweep it costs one more k, or a k one below the best; against k=0 it holds MTP off although it was faster; at Speed up's gate it deletes a copy that was faster. A missed step never picks a slower setup than the one it keeps
size.population: derived for steps between adjacent draft counts on version 1's 8 prompts, at the short depth, on one model (27B AWQ, vLLM, RTX 5090). Applied beyond that: to version 2's added kinds (their spread unmeasured), to Speed up's copy-against-source ratio, and to the long depth (one prompt per document of data/mtp_long_corpus.json, 8 documents: below the count, so a long depth is said underpowered). Each measurement checks its own steps against tolerated_sd (collectors/mtp.size_check). The pooled spread hides kinds that differ: version 1's prompts' own step spreads ran 0.050 (story-lighthouse) to 0.193 (code-intervals) (derivation.json by_prompt_sd)
size.derived: count: the fewest prompts from which core/draft_count.bounds (95% one-sided, paired bootstrap of the median) calls a true +5% step faster and a -5% step slower in at least power of trials, on the per-prompt step deviations (draft_count.step_deviations) of the 2026-11-12 records (280, short depth: the long depth's text looped then). tolerated_sd: the widest step spread at which count still reaches power. valid_from: the fewest prompts at which the rule's false calls (no change called a gain) stay within twice its level; fewer cannot bound a median. power_by_n: the power (the lesser of the two) from valid_from to below count, for the words on a smaller set. docs/evidence/mtp-prompt-count-20261112/derive.py re-derives all of it from records; derivation.json is its output
